title: dual_path_conformance hangs on estate statusline when the suite's stdin never closes
body:
dual_path_conformance's `estate statusline` row blocks forever when the suite's stdin is a stream that never closes.

Found 2026-11-20 by cc on ST0096 WP-01's gate at 298d27f24, under hv decision 69. The test binary sat at 0% CPU for 15 minutes. `sample` shows the one test thread in `via_library -> intent_cli::dispatch -> render::run -> render::estate -> render::estate_statusline -> Stdin::read_to_string -> read`. fd 0 was a unix socket: the gate was started from a Claude Code background shell, whose stdin stays open and never sends EOF.

`estate_statusline` refuses a terminal stdin and reads anything else whole. So the row passes on a tty, because of the refusal, and on `< /dev/null`, because of EOF. It hangs on any stdin that is open but never written, eg a socket or a pipe whose writer stays open. That is the same class as the `mcp` row, which is declared `Hazard::NeverReturns` in dual_path_conformance.rs for this reason. `estate statusline` is probeable and carries no hazard.

WP-01 does not cause this. Its render.rs diff touches neither estate nor statusline, and `estate_statusline` has read stdin this way since b01cec8aa (ST0086 WP-02). The base hangs the same way under the same stdin.

Remedy, for ic's shape and cc's meaning: declare the row's stdin dependence as the `mcp` row does, or give `via_library` a closed stdin for stdin-fed verbs. Either way, a route comparison must not depend on the caller's fds. Until then, start the gate with stdin from /dev/null.
